theory.intro: To change a rate's units, write it as a fraction with $1$ underneath, then rewrite each quantity in the units asked for and simplify back to a unit rate. Top and bottom are converted **separately**, not by the same operation as in a fraction.
facts: Converting to a smaller unit multiplies the number; converting to a larger unit divides it.
Either quantity can change, and a converted denominator goes inside the fraction too: $\frac{\$35}{1\text{ kg}}=\frac{\$35}{(1\times1000)\text{ g}}=\$0.035$/g.
Area units square the length factor: $1$ ha $=10\,000$ m$^2$ and $1$ m$^2=10\,000$ cm$^2$.
Converting the denominator to a **smaller** unit makes the rate number **smaller**, because less happens in each smaller interval.
steps: Write the rate as a fraction with units and $1$ in the denominator.
Convert each quantity to the units required.
Simplify the fraction to a unit rate.

development.solution_text:
$\frac{72\text{ L}}{1\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{(72\times1000)\text{ mL}}{(1\times3600)\text{ s}}$
$=\frac{72\,000\text{ mL}}{3600\text{ s}}$
$=20\text{ mL/s}$

$\frac{\$11}{1\text{ kg}}$
$=\frac{(11\times100)\text{ c}}{(1\times1000)\text{ g}}$
$=\frac{1100\text{ c}}{1000\text{ g}}$
$=1.1\text{ c/g}$

$\frac{6\text{ m}}{1\text{ s}}$
$=\frac{(6\div1000)\text{ km}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{0.006\text{ km}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}$
$=21.6\text{ km/h}$

$\frac{18\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{(18\times1000)\text{ m}}{(1\times3600)\text{ s}}$
$=\frac{18\,000\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}}$
$=5\text{ m/s}$

$\frac{2.4\text{ kg}}{1\text{ L}}$
$=\frac{(2.4\times1000)\text{ g}}{(1\times1000)\text{ mL}}$
$=\frac{2400\text{ g}}{1000\text{ mL}}$
$=2.4\text{ g/mL}$

mastery.question_text:
A crop yield is $16$ t/ha.
Convert it to kg/m$^2$.

A machine dispenses $8.2$ kg/day.
Convert this to g/min, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
$\frac{8.2\text{ kg}}{1\text{ day}}$
$=\frac{(8.2\times1000)\text{ g}}{(1\times1440)\text{ min}}$
$=\frac{8200\text{ g}}{1440\text{ min}}$
$=5.69\text{ g/min}$

mastery.question_text:
A conveyor belt moves at $3$ cm/s.
Convert this rate to m/h.
mastery.solution_text:
$\frac{3\text{ cm}}{1\text{ s}}$
$=\frac{(3\div100)\text{ m}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{0.03\text{ m}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}$
$=108\text{ m/h}$
